SearchAliases: standing in snow and cutting off the arm
Senses.Explanation: Huike's vigil in the snow before Bodhidharma. Huike, still called Shenguang in the account, stands unmoving through a night of heavy snow until it rises above his knees, and Bodhidharma asks, “You have stood long in the snow; what do you seek?” (汝久立雪中，當求何事). Retrospective formulas join “standing in the snow” with “cutting off the arm” (立雪斷臂), transmission of the robe and bowl, and Huike's request for the buddhas' essential way. Later masters preserve conflicting appraisals: Shuwei Tongxuan says, “standing in snow was not yet toil; cutting off the arm was the real thing,” while Bailu Xianduan calls “the Second Patriarch standing in snow to seek mind” unworthy. It also becomes a stock public question—“what is the meaning of the Second Patriarch standing waist-deep in snow?”—to which Jiangshan Faquan answers, “a leap month comes once in three years.” The ordinary weather action has thus become the compact name of a lineage encounter and a recurring interview prompt.
Senses.Note: The allowlisted concordance has 507 matches in 186 texts. This sense covers the full narrative, the fixed standing-snow/cut-arm formula, transmission retrospective, later praise and criticism, and a direct public question. Standing-snow/cut-arm (立雪斷臂), the Second Patriarch standing in snow (二祖立雪), and standing waist-deep in snow (立雪齊腰) all name or appraise the same Huike event. Family revalidation with cutting off the arm (斷臂), facing a wall (面壁), transmitting the robe (傳衣), Huike, and Bodhidharma preserves that event as the Zen-loaded primary sense.

Occurrences.Kwic: 其年十二月九日夜。天大雨雪。光堅立不動。遲明積雪過膝。祖憫而問曰。汝久立雪中。當求何事。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: The Compendium of the Five Lamps (五燈會元), Bodhidharma biography. Bodhidharma is the exact headword-bearing speaker who tells Huike that he has stood long in the snow and asks what he seeks; Huike, still called Shenguang in this part of the account, is the person who stands unmoving until the snow reaches above his knees.

Occurrences.Kwic: 有神光法師，立雪斷臂，堅求諸佛要道，師為易名慧可。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Continued Lamp Record of the Jianzhong Jingguo Era (建中靖國續燈錄), Bodhidharma transmission account. Huike is the exact event actor in the narrative formula that he stood in snow, cut off his arm, and firmly sought the buddhas' essential way.

Occurrences.Kwic: 問。如何是西來的的意。師曰。立雪未為勞。斷臂方為的。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: The Compendium of the Five Lamps (五燈會元): Shuwei Tongxuan answers an unnamed monk's question on the precise intent from the west by saying that standing in the snow was not yet the labor and severing the arm made it exact.

Occurrences.Kwic: 達磨九年面壁，鬼魅之由。二祖立雪求心，飜成不肖。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Strict Lineage of the Five Lamps, volumes 10–25 (五燈嚴統(第10卷-第25卷)), in the explicitly headed section for Chan Master Xianduan of Mount Bailu in Fuzhou (福州白鹿山顯端禪師). Bailu Xianduan is the exact speaker in the hall address who calls Huike's standing in the snow to seek mind an act that ‘turned into unworthiness.’ Bodhidharma and Huike are the named people discussed, not the speaker.

Occurrences.Kwic: 問：二祖立雪齊腰，意旨如何？師曰：三年逢一閏。曰：為甚麼付法傳衣？師曰：村酒足人酤。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: The Complete Book of the Five Lamps, volumes 34–120 (五燈全書(第34卷-第120卷)), Jiangshan Faquan section. An unnamed monk is the exact headword-bearing speaker who asks the meaning of Huike standing in snow to his waist and then asks why the teaching and robe were transmitted; Jiangshan Faquan answers both questions. Senses.Explanation: The physical action of standing in snow, apart from Huike's named event. Zisheng Shengqin answers a question about proceeding within the four deportments with “a heron stands in the snow” (鷺鶿立雪). Danxia Zichun's verse separately compares a heron standing in snow with the bright moon and reed flowers. In these passages the subject is a heron and the phrase denotes its visible posture, not Huike's lineage encounter.
Senses.Note: The heron forms (鷺鶿 and 鷺鷥) are graphic variants within one physical-action family. The direct answer and the verse comparison are different deployments of the same bird-and-snow scene, not further senses.

Occurrences.Kwic: 問四威儀中如何履踐。師曰。鷺鶿立雪。曰恁麼則聞鐘持鉢日上闌干。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Continued Transmission of the Lamp (續傳燈錄), Zisheng Shengqin entry. Zisheng Shengqin is the exact respondent who answers the question about proceeding within the four deportments with 'a heron stands in the snow'; the broad Deshan lineage header does not make Deshan Xuanjian the speaker.

Occurrences.Kwic: 鷺鷥立雪非同色，明月蘆花不似他。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Strict Lineage of the Five Lamps (五燈嚴統(第10卷-第25卷)), in the explicitly headed Danxia Zichun section: Danxia Zichun says, ‘A heron standing in snow is not of the same color; the bright moon and reed flowers are not alike.’ The Jianzhou Jia-clan biography and self-reference to ‘Danxia today’ distinguish him from Danxia Tianran.
